# Review of #346

**Result: block.** Exact head: `7b2cc29be26a9ea5cbf32ed63b677775c8946474`.
One reviewer, one round under amended C34. This covers correctness, cost,
security and privacy together. The author fixes; the prime checks the fix commits
by range-diff, without another review round.

## Blocking findings

| ID | Location | Defect and reproduction | Required correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| B346-R1-01 | `crates/daemon/src/http/pod.rs:303-305,486-524,957-981`; `crates/daemon/src/community/pod.rs:431-457` | **The existing secret brake is bypassed before a public governance commit.** Give `up` a declared parameter whose value matches `first_turn::secret_line`; with `--no-start`, that value is committed even when the first-turn builder rejects it. `set` commits the same value without a secret check, and can subsequently deliver it. Two generated-dummy probes fail with “secret-shaped parameter committed” and “secret-shaped late parameter committed.” No actual credential was read or used. | Apply the existing secret detection before any pod parameter/log/first-turn write or delivery, including unused parameters and `--no-start`. Do not turn a detected-secret refusal into a warning that then persists the secret. This is the existing safety BRAKE, not a new policy. |
| B346-R1-02 | `crates/daemon/src/http/pod.rs:442-459,931-941,970-981`; `crates/daemon/src/community/directory.rs:1518-1550` | **Concurrent successful pod updates lose data.** `open` reads and the mutation constructs a whole replacement document before the writer lock; `write_with` only serializes writing that stale snapshot. Concurrent `set branch=feature/x` and `set subject=updated` both return success, but the final record loses the branch update. The focused concurrent-set probe reproduces it. The same snapshot pattern is used by member changes, down, stages and canary settlement. | Read and modify the current document under the existing writer's serialized build closure, preserving each committed parameter, member, stage, log entry and lifecycle change. Keep the independently owned write's lifetime intact. |
| B346-R1-03 | `crates/daemon/src/http/pod.rs:789-821,1960-1988`; `crates/daemon/src/community/pod.rs:617-623` | **The printed degraded-slot fix cannot work after settlement.** Partially confirm a two-tool slot, wait until it is degraded, then run the prescribed `pod confirm` with both tools. The command succeeds, but `show` remains degraded and `set` keeps skipping it: the one-shot subscriber already exited, and `confirm` only publishes an event. The recovery probe fails with “printed fix did not repair canary.” This strands ordinary pod work even after tools are fixed. | Make a later valid confirmation update the current member's canary state and log through the writer; preserve the one-directional dispatch brake and the bounded initial wait. |
| B346-R1-04 | `crates/daemon/src/http/pod.rs:351-353,369-383,1799-1814`; `crates/daemon/src/community/pod.rs:431-450` | **A supported caller-relative template path is later resolved against a different root.** From a `pods` subdirectory, `up build --no-start --set subject=planning` reads `pods/build` correctly. Subsequent `set build branch=feature/x` refuses because `template_of` tries the repository's `build` path. `recorded_source` is calculated for the response, but the stored document uses the original `Template.source`. The nested-cwd probe reproduces the refusal. | Persist the correctly resolved template reference and use that reference for later reads. Keep explicit path semantics: no template search and no creation of a worktree/branch. |
| B346-R1-05 | `crates/daemon/src/http/pod.rs:1315-1370,1039-1082` | **One running seat can silently belong to two pods.** Create two pods with `--no-start`, add the same running seat to the first and then the second: both records include it. The second add checks only the target pod, not existing membership. The probe fails with “same seat now belongs to two pods.” Taking either pod down then owns a close of the same seat, contrary to req-01 and the other pod's membership/lifecycle. | Preserve a single membership, naming the existing pod and its repair. The packet's warn-only rule and req-01's “refused by a second” wording need reconciliation; a warning must not silently record a second ownership. Serialize this with the membership update. |
| B346-R1-06 | `crates/daemon/src/http/pod.rs:970-975,1041-1044`; `crates/daemon/src/community/pod.rs:742-753` | **A late `work-folder` value is accepted and displayed but ignored by down.** Start without that optional parameter, `set work-folder=<absolute worktree>`, then `down`: the freeze is null with no warning, although the parameter is recorded. `set` changes the parameter row, while down reads the creation-time `meta.work_folder`. The late-folder probe reproduces it. `subject` likewise has two sources that diverge when set later. | Use one current source for operational parameters, or update their operational metadata atomically. A late work-folder must drive the freeze; keep subject/memory semantics consistent. |
| B346-R1-07 | `crates/daemon/src/http/pod.rs:1677-1690,1755-1796` | **Deliverable write-back bypasses the degraded dispatch brake.** In a one-member pod, make the member its deliverable's write-back role, degrade it, then record a stage. Pij creates a role request to that degraded member without warning; the probe reports a non-null write-back request. Routing through a role does not change that this is pij's own dispatch to its member. | Before member-targeted write-back dispatch, honor the same brake and name the skipped degraded member while still recording the stage. Do not prevent direct messages or affect unrelated consulted holders. |
| B346-R1-08 | `crates/cli/src/pod.rs:23-33,35-65` | **Normal CLI output hides the required information and safety warnings.** `set`, `down` and revive return warning strings, but the renderer reads `warning["line"]`, printing `! -`. It ignores member `outcome`, rendering an unsuccessful close as “started”; it also never prints each plan slot's `first_turn`. Two CLI renderer probes fail, including a keep-open warning and a close refusal. JSON-only visibility does not satisfy the ordinary commands' inform-and-warn contract. | Render the actual warning shape and member outcomes, and print the promised plan first turns. Ensure a user sees why a member stayed running and the working repair, without requiring `--json`. |

## Notes, not additional blocks

**B346-R1-09 — Canary ownership and cost declaration.**
`http/pod.rs:789-821` launches a detached task retaining `AppState`, consumes
`pod.canary` events in a `while` loop, and uses `timeout_at` with an absolute
15-minute deadline. It is event-driven, not a poll, and the deadline is bounded.
There is no handle/cancellation registration in pod down or daemon shutdown.
A downed pod can still receive its later settlement commit/FYI; an unanswered
task remains until the bound or stream end. Process exit drops the runtime, but
graceful runtime shutdown does not explicitly join this task. Name this lifecycle
and finite deadline in the cost row instead of claiming “no loop or timer.”
This is a bounded retention/cleanup gap, not evidence of an unbounded launch
loop. Any new hardening outside fixing the approved behavior remains subject
to C35.

**B346-R1-10 — Keep requirement/step/proof states truthful.**
Req-09 correctly remains in-progress, and plan 248 ac-0005 remains unchecked.
Workstream 008 s02 is nevertheless complete although its `done_when` includes
the still-missing live spawn-counter receipt. Reconcile that state. The shipped
claims affected by the blockers are not yet demonstrated, particularly req-01,
req-03, req-05, req-14 and req-19. Plan 249's checked ac-0002 still says template
close steps run, although req-06 explicitly and correctly defers them to
PRD 010. There are also remaining declared-output gaps: wiring is present in
the template schema but not parsed, recorded or shown; the pod first-turn path
helper is unused (first turns are stored at the role); `show` does not include
members' folder or type. `plan` assembles with no slot seed/focus, whereas up
passes the seed to the actual spawn. Reconcile these claims or implement their
approved behavior; do not call schema validation assembled-behavior proof.
The declared `--session` addition is still a C35 approval item, not an inferred
permission from this review.

**B346-R1-11 — Improve the review harness, without adding unsolicited work.**
The existing tests prove creation, an initial canary settlement, and late values
for nondegraded members, but miss the normal-use regressions above. The down
integration test exercises the same close refusal, not a successful stop; the
existing memory-turn HTTP suite supplies the successful-stop/recycled-PID/cold
evidence. Preserve the focused regressions with the fixes, especially the
mutation-killing dispatch test. There is no review procedure in `just proc`'s
nine-procedure inventory. A read-only exact-head review recipe that archives,
runs selectors, captures sanitized receipts, and tests the brake would eliminate
repeated setup inference; propose it under C35 rather than implement it here.

`pij-tmux` suite was not run.

## Cost and security disposition

| Changed path | Rate and scaling |
|---|---|
| Plan/show/history/activity | On demand, in-process reads; no new process launch. Finite per-command loops scale with members, roles and their indexed event history. History reads at most 256 KiB per listed session, 5 MiB per seat at the default 20. |
| Up | Existing spawn path once per successfully started slot; no consulted-seat launch. One existing role-assign commit per slot plus pod creation, member and settlement commits; one canary message per tool-bearing slot. One finite event-consumer task per aggregate up; the individual join path creates one for each tool-bearing join. No recurring polling launch. |
| Set/release/add-existing/stage | One existing writer commit per command, with on-demand deliveries/role requests. Add-role reuses one existing spawn plus its membership commit. |
| Down/revive | Existing close-stop or revive handler once per applicable member. Down adds ONE counted git status read for an absolute recorded work-folder and one pod commit. Existing handler waits/checks are reused, not a new pod polling path. |
| Canary wait | One absolute 15-minute deadline per outstanding task; one iteration per matching canary event until all requested seats answer. Concurrent tasks consume the shared event kind and filter by pod/seat. Zero per-tick process launches. Cleanup limit is B346-R1-09. |

Two live daemon readings at `06:37:56Z` and `06:38:16Z` both show total 1015,
with every per-site counter unchanged (0 launches/s in that interval).
`just spawn-rate --seconds 20` reports 68.9 new processes/s machine-wide and
no sampled daemon children. These are live-current-fleet receipts, not
before/after operation receipts for this undeployed PR; req-09's after-deploy
receipt remains owed.

The spawn-site sensor passes both count coverage and absolute/resolved-path
launch rules; the new freeze uses the existing counted `git.community` helper.
Template reads honor the explicitly supplied path and follow filesystem links;
the PRD permits templates anywhere, and C33 trusts same-user files, so this is
not a new per-seat isolation vulnerability. Session IDs containing `/`, `\`
or `..` are rejected before transcript construction. Tail reads seek from the
end and use `take(TAIL_CAP)`; missing transcripts or absent tail usage report
unknown, and a huge regular transcript never causes a whole-file read. No new
migration/dependency/lockfile source was added. Added-line scans found no
home-directory identity paths, emails or private-key markers. Spawns are
parented to the resolved caller; type text grants no authority beyond role IDs.

Down genuinely calls close-stop's handler, retaining its process-start,
ownership, memory-turn and cold checks; keep-open members are skipped and
consulted rows are not enumerated for stopping. Revive uses its existing
handler and turns cold refusal into a logged warning. The membership defect
must be fixed before that per-pod scope can be relied upon.
